headline: Benchmark choices and inductive biases shape ML drug-response and design models
label: Ml Models For Drug Discovery
summary: Held-out chemistry and out-of-distribution splits are exposing how metric choice and identifiability limit model claims in drug discovery.
synthesis: The dominant thread is generalization under distribution shift in learned models for drug discovery. Several items stress held-out chemistry or cold-start settings: one shows that the evaluation metric alone can reverse model rankings for drug-response transcriptome prediction in unseen chemistry, and another proposes a leakage-aware predictor and lineage-ceiling diagnostic for cancer drug response. Others address out-of-distribution performance directly, through physics-based auxiliary losses for a synthesizability filter, calibrated conformal intervals in a GPU-free design platform, and calibrated hybrid inference for cold-start drug-drug interaction prediction. Foundation-style sequence models appear in Pillbox and dtSFM, the latter trained on 714,747 drug-protein interactions. The work is heterogeneous in scope, but the shared emphasis is on what validation protocols and uncertainty estimates can actually support.
